summary: Linear 3×3 system. The origin is not asymptotically stable (an eigenvalue has zero real part).

methods.name: Eigenvalue method
methods.reason: The system is linear with constant coefficients.

steps.title: Write the general solution
steps.text: Each real eigenvalue gives \(\mathbf{v}e^{\lambda t}\); a complex pair \(\alpha \pm \beta i\) gives two real solutions from the real and imaginary parts of \(\mathbf{v}e^{\lambda t}\).
latex: x(t) = C_{2} \sin{\left(t \right)} - C_{3} \cos{\left(t \right)},\qquad y(t) = C_{2} \cos{\left(t \right)} + C_{3} \sin{\left(t \right)},\qquad z(t) = C_{1} e^{- t}

steps.title: Apply the initial conditions
steps.text: Set \(t = 0\) and solve the equations for the constants.

steps.title: Stability
steps.text: The origin is not asymptotically stable (an eigenvalue has zero real part).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked by substituting back into every equation, and it meets the initial conditions.

methods.name: Matrix exponential
methods.reason: For a constant matrix the solution is the matrix exponential applied to the initial vector.

steps.title: Use the matrix exponential
steps.text: The solution of \(\mathbf{X}' = A\mathbf{X}\) is \(\mathbf{X} = e^{At}\mathbf{X}(0)\).

steps.title: Multiply by the initial vector
